> **Beta software — bugs are expected.** Features and compatibility are still being tested. Back up your Minecraft world before pasting structures, and [report bugs](https://github.com/OpenNerdz/mazeforge/issues).

MazeForge designs weathered walls and seeded mazes for Minecraft Java Edition, with a local 3D preview and WorldEdit schematic export.

### Download and launch

Choose your desktop download below, **extract the entire folder**, then double-click the app. Your default browser opens automatically. **No Python installation, coding, terminal commands or account is needed.**

| System | Download | Open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows 10/11, x64 | [Windows ZIP](https://github.com/OpenNerdz/mazeforge/releases/download/v2.0.1-beta.2/mazeforge-2.0.1-beta.2-windows-x64.zip) | MazeForge.exe |
| Mac with Apple Silicon | [Apple Silicon ZIP](https://github.com/OpenNerdz/mazeforge/releases/download/v2.0.1-beta.2/mazeforge-2.0.1-beta.2-macos-arm64.zip) | MazeForge.app |
| Mac with Intel | [Intel Mac ZIP](https://github.com/OpenNerdz/mazeforge/releases/download/v2.0.1-beta.2/mazeforge-2.0.1-beta.2-macos-x64.zip) | MazeForge.app |
| Linux, x64 | [Linux archive](https://github.com/OpenNerdz/mazeforge/releases/download/v2.0.1-beta.2/mazeforge-2.0.1-beta.2-linux-x64.tar.gz) | MazeForge |

**First launch:** these beta builds are unsigned. Windows SmartScreen or macOS Privacy & Security may require approval; Linux file managers may ask permission to launch an executable. Approve only a download you trust; do not disable system protections. Completely prompt-free launch cannot be guaranteed.

Desktop builds are tested on Windows, macOS 15 (both architectures) and Ubuntu 22.04. Linux requires glibc 2.35+ and a desktop browser; Alpine/musl and ARM Linux are not supported by these binaries. Use a current Chrome, Edge or Firefox browser with WebGL 2 enabled.

Choose **More → Quit MazeForge** to stop the app. Closing a browser tab leaves it running; double-clicking the app again reopens it. Settings, exports and imported textures stay in your own application data folder across updates.

### What changed

**Workspace**

- Messages and tooltips appear above open dialogs instead of behind their dimmed backdrop.
- Enter in a dialog field runs its main action (Save, Load, Export) instead of closing the dialog.
- The Save dialog offers **Download .schem**; the seed browser can page back; batch export stops when closed and reports failures.
- Ctrl+S works from text fields, and single-key shortcuts no longer act behind an open dialog.
- Every control works from the keyboard, including settings sections, seed thumbnails and the block picker (Esc closes it, Enter picks the first match).
- Phones: the block count card is visible again, dialogs fit the screen, and New seed, Undo and Redo are in the **More** menu.
- Medium-width windows no longer cut off the settings tabs; slider fills match their values; help text has higher contrast.

**Reliability**

- Designs too large for a browser tab stop with a clear message instead of running out of memory.
- A damaged `.schem` file is rejected at once instead of freezing the page; opened files are preview-only.
- Moss carpet is left out for Minecraft versions before 1.17.
- The local server copes with unreadable folders, no longer lists Windows folders twice, and answers missing files properly.

**Speed**

- Designs build 15–50% faster and their 3D preview is built about 30% faster, with identical output.

### Compatibility

Use Minecraft Java Edition with a matching WorldEdit build. The importer expects modern client archives with version metadata (1.14+); not every version has been tested. Texture matching alone does not establish schematic compatibility. Legacy Java, Bedrock and `.litematic` are not supported.

### Validation

[Checks](https://github.com/OpenNerdz/mazeforge/actions/runs/{{CHECKS_RUN}}) and [Desktop builds](https://github.com/OpenNerdz/mazeforge/actions/runs/{{DESKTOP_RUN}}) passed for commit `{{COMMIT}}`: lint, type checks, dependency audit, secret scans, generation and schematic tests, and HTTP boundary tests on Windows, macOS and Linux. Each desktop executable passed startup with Python removed from PATH, local texture persistence, saving, relaunch and shutdown on its native build platform.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` covers all downloads. The source ZIP without an OS name is also included for developers and requires Python 3.10+. See the README for local data locations and troubleshooting.
